question: Does the articulated Panda arm reproduce the finger stall?
answer: NO. Variant D, the exact Panda chain with exact per-joint controllers and no table/cube/camera/collision, traverses the finger's full 0-40 mm stroke. The arm-chain hypothesis is FALSIFIED as the cause.

rows.result: NOT READABLE - world robot_ci_pick_place advertised no joint_state within the 14 s window; world name was wrong on the first attempt and fixed, but the topic still did not appear. No conclusion drawn.

not_run: D2 exact chain, no arm controllers

signature_observed.reading: The error is negative and SHRINKS monotonically as the command rises, and qdot alternates +/-0.1997 m/s against a declared velocity limit of 0.2 m/s. That is a velocity-limit limit cycle, identical in shape to the "10x velocity limit" limit cycle seen in Part 1B -- not a mechanical stall at a fixed position.
signature_observed.consequence: The finger is not blocked at 21 mm by a static reaction. It is rate-limited and still converging when the sample is taken. Whatever produces the full Panda's flat ~21 mm stall is therefore NOT the arm chain and NOT present in variant D.

what_variant_D_still_lacks_versus_the_fa: the table (the project world places the pads millimetres above it, per world.py comment)
the real robot placement in the scene
next_single_experiment: Make the project-world run readable (the world robot_ci_pick_place loads more plugins and needs longer than 14 s, or the robot model name differs) and command the finger there with the cube removed. That is the failing episode minus the object, and it is the only configuration left that contains the table.
collisions_falsified_at_full_scale: Restoring all eleven gripper and arm link collisions to variant D changes nothing: max q 38.604 mm -> 38.597 mm, final error -1.396 mm -> -1.403 mm. Candidates 11 and 12 are falsified again, now at the scale of the real chain rather than a minimal model.
